# UnreliableRemoteEvent

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("UnreliableRemoteEvent")`

A `RemoteEvent` for data that is sent many times per second and replaced each time. Use it for the positions of a horde, the direction a player aims in or a boss's health, and never for anything that must arrive.

A message is sent once and can be lost. It is not sent again, so a lost message delays nothing else, whereas a lost reliable message makes every later reliable message wait for it.

The newest message wins. A message that arrives after a later one is dropped instead of being delivered late, across all of the game's unreliable events, so a script never receives a message older than one it already received.

A message to a machine that does not have the event yet, or where no handler is connected, is dropped.

The arguments are limited to 16 KiB; a larger message raises an error at the call. A message larger than about 1 KB is sent in several packets and is lost entirely if any of them is, so large messages are lost more often. Send small messages, or several that are each useful alone.

In every other respect it behaves like `RemoteEvent`: the values it accepts, who can call which method, and how the authority identifies the sender.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Methods

### `FireAllClients(arguments: ...any)`

Sends the arguments to every player's machine once, including a host's own. Only the authority can call it; it raises an error on a client.

### `FireClient(player: Player, arguments: ...any)`

Sends the arguments to one player's machine once. If the message arrives, `ClientReceived` fires there. Only the authority can call it; it raises an error on a client.

### `FireServer(arguments: ...any)`

Sends the arguments to the authority once. If the message arrives, `ServerReceived` fires there with this machine's player followed by the arguments. On an authority that has a player of its own, the event fires locally. Raises an error on a dedicated server, which has no player.

### `FireServerFor(player: Player, arguments: ...any)`

Sends a message to the authority on behalf of one of this machine's local players, on a machine that is itself the authority. `ServerReceived` fires with that player. Raises an error on a client, and for a remote player or a guest that has been removed. `FireServer` always sends as the primary local player.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `ClientReceived(arguments: ...any)`

Fires on a player's machine when a message arrives that the authority sent with `FireClient` for that player or with `FireAllClients`.

### `LocalClientReceived(player: Player, arguments: ...any)`

Fires on a machine with local guests when the authority sends a message to one of its guest players. Passes that player, followed by the arguments. Messages to the primary player and to all clients fire `ClientReceived` instead.

### `ServerReceived(player: Player, arguments: ...any)`

Fires on the authority when a message that a player's machine sent with `FireServer` arrives. Passes the player who sent it, followed by the arguments. Treat the arguments as claims by the client and validate them.
